title: Rank, column space, and row space
section: Vector Spaces ▷ The Rank, Column Space, and Row Space
terms: rank; row rank; column rank; row space; column space; pivot column; full rank.

exposition.text:
m n
For an m × n matrix, the column space lies in R and the row space in R . Their dimensions
agree; the common number is the rank, at most min(m, n). The equation Ax = b is consistent
exactly when b lies in the column space.
Row reduction preserves row space and rank, so the nonzero rows of an echelon matrix form
a row-space basis. It generally changes column space: use the pivot columns of the original
T
matrix to obtain a column-space basis. Equivalently row-reduce A to obtain column-space
information. Full rank means rank min(m, n), not necessarily invertibility for a rectangular
matrix.

The identities Row(A) = Col(A ) and Col(A) = Row(A ) also give membership tests. If

A y = 0, every vector in the column space is perpendicular to y; hence y b ̸= 0 proves that
Ax = b is inconsistent.

Let A = 2 4 6 . For which b is (1, b, 0) in its column space?
 
1 1 1
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) Every real b

solution.text:
The second row is twice the first, so every image has second coordinate twice its first. Thus
b = 2 is necessary. The first and third rows are independent, so this single constraint is also
sufficient.

form a basis for its column space?
(A) Columns 1,2 (B) Columns 1, 2, 3
(C) Columns 1, 2, 4 (D) Columns 2, 3
(E) All four columns

solution.text:
The pivot columns are 1, 2, 4. Those columns of the original matrix are independent and
span its column space. Column 3 equals twice column 1 minus column 2.

question.text:
Which operation necessarily preserves the column space of A?
(A) Replacing a column by zero
(B) Right multiplication by an invertible matrix
(C) Left multiplication by every invertible matrix
(D) Deleting a pivot column
(E) Transposing A

solution.text:
−1
The columns of AB are combinations of those of A. If B is invertible, A = (AB)B gives
the reverse containment, hence the column spaces coincide.

(B) Ax = b has infinitely many solutions.
(C) Ax = b has no solution.
(D) A has full row rank.

solution.text:
T T T T
If Ax = b, then y b = y Ax = (A y) x = 0, contradicting the given value one. A vector
orthogonal to every column but not to b certifies that b lies outside the column space.
